This feels incredibly disingenuous, or at best willfully ignorant. Conflating the loss of jobs with the complete eradication of them is intentionally misrepresenting the issue. Look at brick and mortar stores, malls, and you can see the shuttering of many as a direct result of the availability of online shopping. How many of your stores removed checkout aisles for self service, if not entirely? Do you think they reassigned the elders there to shelf stocking? There are going to be- there has already been- jobs lost as a result of AI, people whose roles did not universally disappear but no longer exist, or exist at smaller scale, in companies choosing to use AI. What’s most insidious though is that AI is taking jobs before people can even get them through automated resume screening, through “interviews”, by removing all human aspect and relying on an algorithm that in some cases has bypassed qualified candidates that had to actually call the hiring manager after being rejected only to then be offered the role. No one believes the positions that are competing against ai are going to become obsolete. But they’re going to become far less available which for a generation of people, who planned and built their lives set towards that career, is devastating. AI as a tool should never be used, in its current state, to blindly replace humans. The same way kitchen knives, as a tool, should never be used to hurt people. People that wield them with ill intent will abuse their use and the effect that it will have is real.

Linus Torvalds has said the following: Previously, Torvalds was skeptical of the AI hype, but in July 2026 he made his position much clearer on the Linux kernel mailing list: Linux is not an anti-AI project. AI is clearly a useful tool. In his view, it's no longer realistic to claim that AI has no value in software development. He also said that if someone opposes AI tools on principle, they are free to fork the project or simply leave. He also noted that AI can spot embarrassing bugs made by humans, and that human intelligence isn't perfect either.
